comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: The seeded ledger row records a RED run as a green "2/2 solved" pipeline proof — and its numbers are impossible under this PR's own tooling**

Three independent problems with the seed row (`bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json:11-24`, rendered at `README.md:109-116`):

**1. The run is not green.** Run [40023718645](https://api.github.com/repos/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/40023718645) concluded **`failure`** — the `Package submission` and `Summary & verdict` steps both failed (verified via the Actions API during this review). This PR's own aggregate step says: *"Runs only on a GREEN aggregate (the verdict + Tier-0 `submit verify` passed) — a partial or failing run never lands"*, and `pbench_record.py`'s docstring says the ledger is written *"on every GREEN run"*. The Tier-0 verify never ran for this run — its numbers were never validated by the gate the PR builds.

**2. The per-instance numbers contradict the repo's own solved convention.** `pbench_record.read_stats` (lines 100-104) and `bench/programbench/summary.py:19-20,38-43` define `solved = every scored test true` — i.e. `solved: true` **implies** `score_pct == 100.0` ("a 100-after-rounding instance that isn't solved is NOT solved"). The seed asserts `98.0%` **and** `solved: true` for both instances; the README consequently renders `| cmatrix | 98.0% | 506 | ✅ |` and a headline `Solved 2/2` — self-contradictory on its face.

**3. `98.0` cannot even be produced by the tool for these test counts.** `round(100.0*passed/len(tests), 1)` yields `98.0` for **no** integer passed-count with 680 tests (667→98.1, 666→97.9); for 506 tests it implies 496/506 passed → `solved: false`. So this row was not produced by `read_stats` from a packaged `_stats/` (which also never existed — `submit package` failed).

Since the PR's entire deliverable is *honest, committed, self-reported* results (gh-182 R1), the first published row must satisfy the honesty contract it establishes. Please either re-run the smoke dispatch to a **green** aggregate and record that run via the tool, or fix the seed to match the run's actual packaged `_stats` (correct `score_pct` with `solved` derived by the tool's rule, or drop the row). Also note the missing `fa_version` — a recorded row would carry `--fa-version` (renders `—` today).

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: The "Score" column is labeled pass@1 but shows a different metric**

`render_row_table` fills the Score column with `score_pct` — the **unweighted mean of per-instance test-pass percentages** (`read_stats`: `100 × passed/len(tests)` averaged in `upsert`) — while the Mode column says *"full — pass@1, all N instances"* and the section intro says *"Pass@1: one attempt per instance"*. Those are different numbers: summary.py's headline pass@1 convention is the **instance-solved fraction** (`Solved {n}/{len} — headline pass@1 over the full official set`), and the official ProgramBench board ranks the same way.

The seeded row already shows the drift: Mode reads "pipeline proof", Score reads `98.0%` (mean test-pass rate), while pass@1 for that row would be `2/2 = 100%`. On a full run the gap grows (one 40% instance among 201 barely moves a tests-weighted mean but visibly moves the solved fraction). A reader comparing this table against the official board will misread every row.

Suggest one of:
- record/display the solved fraction (`solved/attempted`) as Score to match the pass@1 headline, or
- rename the column to what it is (e.g. `Test-pass %`) and say in the section intro that it is the mean per-instance scored-test rate.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Re-running an old green run silently regresses the committed ledger**

This step records and pushes the ledger **from the run's pinned checkout**: `actions/checkout` (top of the job) pins the dispatch-time sha, so the working tree holds the ledger **as it was when the run was dispatched**. The record → render → `git push` chain then writes that whole stale tree back:

- Run A dispatched at sha S1 (ledger L0) → records L0+A → pushes.
- Run B dispatched later at S2 (ledger L0+A) → records L0+A+B → pushes.
- Someone clicks **"Re-run all jobs"** on run A months later → checkout is S1 again → the step records **L0+A**, regenerates the README section from it, and pushes — **B's row (and any hand-backfilled rows) silently disappear from the public board**, and the README section rewinds with them.

The `concurrency` group serializes *concurrent* runs but does nothing against this cross-time overwrite. The gh-1682 sibling step (`bench-harbor.yml` "Update leaderboard ledger & table") has the same shape, so this is a copied pattern — but this PR is the moment to harden it cheaply, e.g.:

```bash
git fetch origin "${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}"
git rebase "FETCH_HEAD"   # or: check out the branch's ledger before recording
```

before `pbench_record.py` runs (a non-fast-forward push rejection failing the step would already be better than a silent revert). Worth a follow-up for the harbor step too.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: Artifact links expire with the retention window — say so (or extend it)**

The ledger rows link the `programbench-submission` artifact (`…/runs/<id>/artifacts/<artifact-id>`), and the renderer presents them as the lasting analysis surface ("the run's value survives the CI artifact retention window and stays reachable" — `pbench_render.py` docstring). But the artifact itself **expires** on the default retention schedule (the seeded run's artifact shows `expired: false` today; it will 404 later), so README and fa1.dev will accumulate dead links while the run links stay alive.

Cheap options:
- add `retention-days:` (e.g. `365`) to the pre-existing "Upload submission folder" step so trajectories/eval logs outlive the default window;
- and/or have the renderer note "(artifact link expires with GitHub's retention window)" so the page stays honest after expiry.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `read_stats` dies with an uncaught `TypeError` on null/non-numeric cost or calls entries**

`float(costs[iid])` / `int(calls[iid])` raise `TypeError` for a JSON `null` or a string value in `cost.json`/`calls.json`, and `main` only catches `(OSError, ValueError)` around `read_stats` — so a malformed stats file produces a raw traceback instead of the tool's clean `error: … ` exit-2 path (the same file class that gets the friendly `FileNotFoundError` treatment two lines up). Since `summary.py` writes these files it's unlikely in CI, but hand-backfills and future format drift hit this path. Guard with `isinstance(costs[iid], (int, float))` / drop the entry, or add `TypeError` to the caught set — a one-line test (`cost.json` with `{"cmatrix": null}`) pins it.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: HTML page drops the run-page fallback in an edge case the Markdown render handles** Here the fallback is suppressed whenever `artifact_urls` is **non-empty**, even if no entry actually rendered a link — compare `render_detail_blocks` (Markdown), which collects `links` filtered by `a.get("url")` and falls back when *no link was rendered*. A hand-edited ledger row like `"artifact_urls": [{"label": "programbench-submission"}]` (url lost in a merge) therefore renders the HTML page with **no artifact link and no run-page fallback**, while the README section for the same row still shows the run-page link. Reuse the Markdown condition: emit the fallback when no artifact `

` was appended.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `splice_readme` duplicates the block when the begin marker is orphaned, and hardcodes one trailing char**

Two edge cases in the splice:

1. If `MARKER_BEGIN` exists but `MARKER_END` is missing or precedes it (a merge-conflict remnant of the generated region is the classic way), the function falls through to the anchor/heading insertion and appends a **second** generated block next to the orphaned one — the README then carries two ProgramBench sections and `--check` can never converge. Failing loudly (exit 2, "orphaned pbench-leaderboard:begin marker") would surface the corrupt README immediately.
2. `text[end + len(MARKER_END) + 1:]` assumes exactly one character (the `\n`) after the end marker; a marker at EOF without a trailing newline would silently swallow the following character into the replaced span. `text.find("\n", end)` with an EOF fallback is the robust form.

Neither bites the committed README today (the round-trip test covers the healthy shape) — this is cheap armor for the CI-only writer.

comments.body:
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The seeded ProgramBench ledger row publishes a RED run ([40023718645](https://api.github.com/repos/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/40023718645) — `Package submission` + `Summary & verdict` failed) as a green "Solved 2/2 ✅ … 98.0%" pipeline proof, with numbers the PR's own tooling cannot produce. Two important issues (Score column mislabeled pass@1; a stale re-run can silently regress the committed ledger) and four suggestions round it out.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json:14` — seed row violates the PR's own green-only contract and `summary.py`'s ✅ convention (98.0% + `solved: true` is impossible per `read_stats`; 680 tests cannot round to 98.0) — see comment1
- ⚠️ `bench/leaderboard/pbench_render.py:122` — "Score" shows mean per-instance test-pass % while the Mode column says pass@1 (comment2)
- ⚠️ `.github/workflows/bench-programbench.yml:750` — re-running an old green run regenerates the ledger from its stale checkout and drops rows recorded since (comment3; the gh-1682 harbor step shares the shape)
- 💡 artifact links expire with the retention window; `read_stats` uncaught `TypeError` on null costs; HTML fallback asymetry; `splice_readme` orphan-marker edge (comments 4-7)

**Next Steps**:
1. Re-derive the seed from the run's actual `_stats` (or re-run to a green aggregate and record that) so `score_pct`/`solved` agree with the tool's math
2. Align or relabel the Score metric with the pass@1 headline; guard the record step against stale-checkout ledger pushes
3. Sweep the four suggestions
